This supports H-MAPPING-GAP and H-LOC-CODE-UNRECOGNIZED, redefining the root problem (PD-1) as a systematic code/mapping mismatch rather than fixable data errors or carrier flakiness.

The DEFINE gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-criticality unknowns (U-UNK-SAMPLE-SIZE, U-UNK-RULE-OWNER) into verification obligations VOB-U-UNK-SAMPLE-SIZE and VOB-U-UNK-RULE-OWNER, both of which remain OPEN at release time.

What was actually released (SD-1.release_scope) is limited to two work items: quantifying the full reject population and diagnosing the LOC_UNKNOWN root cause (both marked DONE). The actual mapping fix for process P-1 and clarification of ORG-B's validation rules with SH-INT were not part of this release.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no items held back further (hold: []), meaning the two unresolved work items (quantification/diagnosis) proceed to release despite open verification obligations and unresolved internal contradictions flagged by the harness's semantic checks.
limitations_explained: A semantic consistency check (data_asset_completeness_consistency) found that DA-REJ's completeness field is recorded as COMPLETE, yet assumption A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE and unknown/obligation U-UNK-SAMPLE-SIZE/VOB-U-UNK-SAMPLE-SIZE all treat DA-REJ's completeness as UNKNOWN to justify deferring the sample-size fix; this is an unresolved internal contradiction in the record, not merely a caveat.

A second semantic check (work_item_done_vs_unknown_open) found that work item W-WI-1-QUANTIFY-FULL-POPULATIO is marked DONE and claims the 3-record E-01 sample was replaced by a full-population query, but U-UNK-SAMPLE-SIZE and VOB-U-UNK-SAMPLE-SIZE remain OPEN/DEFERRED and SD-1's unfinished_scope still lists the 3-sample limitation as unresolved.

Two HIGH-impact verification obligations are still OPEN and block scope beyond this release: VOB-U-UNK-SAMPLE-SIZE (blocking fix_location_code_mapping:P-1 and resubmit_shipment_notices:H-1) and VOB-U-UNK-RULE-OWNER (blocking fix_location_code_mapping:P-1 and clarify_validation_rules:SH-INT).

The mapping/validation-configuration fix for P-1 itself is unfinished; without SH-INT's rule documentation (which is itself VOB-blocked), it cannot yet be determined whether the mismatch originates in ORG-A's codes or ORG-B's rule configuration.
Even after a full population query, EVENT_ORDER would remain under-evidenced by only 1 sample record, because resolving sample-size representativeness does not, by itself, resolve causal attribution.
The DEFINE gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, with the deferred critical unknowns tracked as verification obligations rather than resolved before release.
proposal.summary: Problem PD-1: shipment notices sent from ORG-A to ORG-B (handoff H-1, process P-1) are being rejected, and the sampled reject-log evidence (E-01) shows the rejects cluster into systematic reason codes (2/3 LOC_UNKNOWN, 1/3 EVENT_ORDER; F-01-F-03) rather than scattered correctable errors or transient carrier flakiness as the requester (SH-REQ) initially claimed (CL-01, CL-02). That initial 'AI auto-fix and resubmit' framing was tested as a hypothesis and rejected (H-FIXABLE-DATA-ERRORS: REJECTED); the carrier-flakiness claim remains unsupported beyond a non-authoritative stakeholder statement. The release delivers only the population-quantification and root-cause-diagnosis work (SD-1.release_scope), while the DEFINE gate's CONDITIONAL_PASS left two HIGH-impact verification obligations (sample representativeness, rule ownership) open, and the harness's own semantic checks flagged unresolved contradictions between what is marked DONE/COMPLETE and what the unknowns say is still open. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no items held) given the production of useful diagnostic findings, with the mapping fix for P-1 and the carrier-flakiness/causal-attribution questions left unresolved for later work.
